ordered_diagnoses: diffuse systemic sclerosis with bullous lesions

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion and associated skin changes
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral and involves the right thigh and buttock
Recent limitation of motion in the right limb joint
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings included normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Alcian blue staining was negative

differentials: diffuse systemic sclerosis with bullous lesions

shortlist: diffuse systemic sclerosis with bullous lesions

shortlist.label: en coup de sabre scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: matches unilateral skin hardening and limited joint motion

shortlist.label: scleromyxedema
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with skin hardening and increased density of fibroblasts

shortlist.label: diffuse systemic sclerosis with bullous lesions
shortlist.why_kept: possible explanation for progressive skin hardening and joint limitation

shortlist.label: sclerodactyly
shortlist.why_kept: related to scleroderma and could explain skin hardening

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening, limited to one side of the body, along with the histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts and the absence of inflammation, is most consistent with en coup de sabre scleroderma, a form of localized scleroderma.

rejected.label: scleromyxedema
rejected.why: Scleromyxedema typically presents with widespread lichenoid papules and mucin deposition, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: diffuse systemic sclerosis with bullous lesions
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by widespread skin thickening and systemic involvement, which is not present in this patient.

rejected.label: poikiloderma
rejected.why: Poikiloderma is characterized by a combination of atrophy, telangiectasia, and pigmentary changes, which does not match the patient's presentation of skin hardening and fibrosis.

rejected.label: sclerodactyly
rejected.why: Sclerodactyly refers to the thickening and hardening of the skin of the fingers, which is not the primary location of the patient's symptoms.
